study.title: Kernelytics: Multispectral Drone Imagery and Deep Learning for Early Corn Assessment
study.short_title: Kernelytics: Multispectral Drone Deep Learning for Early Corn
study.venue: 2023 IEEE MIT Undergraduate Research Technology Conference (URTC)

segmentation.best_model: U-Net ResNet-101, composite 5-band, tile 32x32 (corn F1 0.66, non-corn F1 0.98)

dataset.name: Phantom 4 Multispectral orthomosaic of Roundup Ready corn, Creggan Hill Farm, Troupsburg NY (Kernelytics)
dataset.note: DJI Phantom 4 Multispectral (6 sensors: RGB, Red, Red Edge, Blue, Green, NIR), 7.62-acre field, juvenile corn 4 in, data 2023-06-20, 655 images with 2 cm/px GSD at 38.1 m, Pix4D orthomosaic then tiled to chips; labels: 625 corn bboxes, 1500 corn + 1200 weed pixel segments; trained in ArcGIS with 90-10 split, NMS 0.2.

F1.ambiguity: Per-class F1 reported instead: corn 0.66, non-corn 0.98 (tile 32).

PA.ambiguity: Overall pixel accuracy not stated; separate weed-segmentation U-Net reported 98% accuracy.

weed_F1.ambiguity: Separate U-Net for weeds reported segmentation ACCURACY of 98% (not F1).

crop_F1.quote: The U-Net model with the composite band and an image chip tile size of 32x32 pixels had the best performance for corn segmentation.
crop_F1.ambiguity: Corn class F1 = 66% at tile 32x32 (composite bands); non-corn F1 = 98%. Values from a conference table; validation-set metrics on a small annotated field (1,500 corn + 1,200 weed segments).

issues: Undergraduate research-conference paper; small annotated set and modest metrics quality.
No mIoU/overall accuracy; per-class F1 (corn 0.66, non-corn 0.98 at 32x32) and separate weed-segmentation accuracy 98%.
